purpose: Tildrakizumab-asmn is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults. It helps clear up the thick, scaly patches on your skin that psoriasis causes. It is used when other treatments have not worked well enough or are not a good option for you.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called IL-23 that causes the inflammation responsible for psoriasis flares. This medication works by blocking that specific protein, which helps calm down the overactive immune response. By reducing that inflammation, your skin has a chance to heal and clear up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include injection site reactions such as redness or pain where the shot is given, upper respiratory infections like a common cold, and diarrhea. Some people may also experience back pain or tiredness.
warnings: Because this medication affects your immune system, it may make it harder for your body to fight infections, so tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of infection such as fever, chills, or unusual cough. Your doctor will check you for tuberculosis (TB) before starting this medicine. Avoid live vaccines while on this medication. Let your healthcare provider know all other medications you take, and always tell them if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually by a healthcare provider. You will typically receive a starting dose at week 0, another dose at week 4, and then one dose every 12 weeks (about every 3 months) after that. Each dose is 100 mg.
